chapter: Life in France and Sidney Bechet
title: Bechet's fame in France compared with his own recognition
summary: Bechet was a national hero with a bust and street named for him; Waters says he is content with late recognition and now earns good concert money in France.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: How would you compare his reception in France, in which he was virtually made a national - he was made a national hero - with yours?
He's got a great big bust down there in -
in Juan Les Pins. Either Juan Les Pins or one of those towns down there -
Yeah. There it is, the street in Paris named after him, right, Rue de la Bechet?
Also, I played it. I played that s-, I played that, at La Parisienne [?] -
Yeah, I played it, because it was in Nancy.
How would you compare Bechet's reception in Europe with yours?
Well I - well, he was bigger than me, see.
Uh huh. Were you disappointed that, or were you satisfied with your reception in Europe?

Sure, I was satisfied, I'm not jealous or nothing, you know. I'm not a guy that [if] somebody else has a big success I'm worried or jealous, you know? I figure I get my - which I did. I mean it's very, I'm very happy, see, Phil, to get my recognition ear-, late. It's better for me to get it late than even earlier, you see. Now I have more, I work more in France than I ever worked in my life. And just like I show you, the money isn't bad. When I first went there you know what it was, you weren't getting no six or seven hundred dollars for 45 minutes, you know what I mean? Because I had worked the Cigalle and oh, so-and-so-and-so-and-so, you know, one of those things. But now I get paid 'cause I can afford to refuse other things too, you know, see. But I'm always ask-, they're always asking me for, to work. But the money's slow and then I just don't do it, see, you know? But I could be workin' all the time in that joint. Now I think the things that, that is interesting, you know? I wouldn't take a steady job like with Cigalle again, even - especially if they couldn't pay that kind of money, no way, you know. A club date is not like a concert or a festival. So I couldn't afford to take it because it's too hard for them.
